# `actors`

Group: **Traffic**. What moves and what transmits: the fleet, its size, roadside units and the backend.

118 settings. The status column says whether editing a setting changes a run; see [how to read these tables](../overview.md). Paths use `[]` for a list element and `*` for a map key.

| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-gnss-burst-rate-hz"></span>`actors.vehicles.gnss.burst_rate_hz` | number | Hz | | [0, 0.5]<br>recommended 0.006 per second (default); higher for a dense downtown. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How often a degraded burst (multipath, an urban canyon) starts, per second. Unset is 0.006. How often a stretch of poor positioning starts, as among tall buildings. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-gnss-outage-probability"></span>`actors.vehicles.gnss.outage_probability` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended 0 (default) to 0.05. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The chance each fix is lost entirely. Unset is 0. The chance each position fix is lost altogether, as in a tunnel. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-gnss-smoothing-tau-s"></span>`actors.vehicles.gnss.smoothing_tau_s` | number | s | | [0, 600]<br>recommended 100 s (the US real-world presets, RTCA DO-229's smoothing constant); 0 for raw fixes. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The receiver's position-smoothing time constant, seconds: the receiver propagates its solution with its own Doppler velocity and blends each raw fix in at this time constant, as deployed receivers do (`gnss/error/gauss-markov` module docs). Unset or 0 outputs every raw fix, whose white noise makes consecutive 10 Hz BSMs disagree by metres. How slowly the GPS receiver blends new fixes into the position it reports, steering by its own measured speed in between, as real receivers do. 0 reports every raw fix, which jumps by metres between messages. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-gnss-static-hold-mps"></span>`actors.vehicles.gnss.static_hold_mps` | number | m/s | | [0, 1.5]<br>recommended 0.3 m/s (the US real-world presets); 0 for off. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The receiver's static-hold threshold, m/s: below this measured speed it holds its position and reports zero velocity. Unset or 0 is off; read only with `smoothing_tau_s`. Below this speed the GPS receiver treats the vehicle as stopped: it holds the position and reports zero speed. Needs the smoothing. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-gnss-velocity-noise-mps"></span>`actors.vehicles.gnss.velocity_noise_mps` | number | m/s | | [0, 0.5]<br>recommended Unset (default) to compare with earlier runs; 0 with the BSM timing model on, whose fitted output noise then carries the message-level speed and heading noise. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The receiver's velocity output noise, m/s per horizontal axis, drawn afresh at every fix. Unset is the GPS SPS committed velocity accuracy (0.2 m/s at 95 %, σ 0.102 m/s), which as a white 10 Hz noise makes consecutive BSMs' speeds differ by sd 0.14 m/s, where CV-pilot locked devices' differ by 0.045 m/s. 0 leaves the BSM-level speed and heading noise to `bsm_timing`'s fitted `output_noise`. How much the GPS receiver's reported speed jitters from one fix to the next. Unset uses the GPS service's 95 % accuracy figure, which makes consecutive messages' speeds differ about three times more than real CV-pilot units' do. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-gnss-stated-sigma-m"></span>`actors.vehicles.gnss.stated_sigma_m` | number | m | | [0, 12.7]<br>recommended Unset (default) to compare with earlier runs; 0.3 m (Tampa CV pilot) or 2.0 m (Orem) to match a deployment. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The one-sigma horizontal accuracy the receiver states in each BSM's J2735 `PositionalAccuracy.semiMajor`, metres (the median over devices). Unset or 0 states the model's own honest 95 % radius (about 6.5 m with raw fixes, 5.1 m smoothed). Deployed OBUs state far less than their real error: the CV-pilot medians are 0.30 m Tampa, 0.40 m NYC, 0.50 m Wyoming and a constant 2.00 m Orem (measured with tools/realdata). The position accuracy each car's radio claims in its messages (one standard deviation). Unset claims the receiver's true error statistics; real deployed units claim much less than their real error, which makes detectors that trust the claim stricter. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-gnss-stated-sigma-log-sd"></span>`actors.vehicles.gnss.stated_sigma_log_sd` | number | | | [0, 3]<br>recommended 0.81 with 0.3 m (Tampa's spread); 0 with 2.0 m (Orem's units all claim the same). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The per-device spread of that stated accuracy: a lognormal's log-sd, drawn once per receiver. Unset or 0 states the median on every device; Tampa's per-device medians give 0.81. How much the claimed accuracy differs from one car to the next. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-enabled"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.enabled` | boolean | | | recommended Off (default) to compare with earlier runs; on for honest-trigger studies. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Turns the model on. Unset or false is off (every existing run unchanged). Gives each car's radio its own message timing, as real units have: some stamp each message with the instant of the GPS fix (locked), others do not (free), and those now and then send a position one fix too old or too new, or the last one again. Real CV-pilot data shows that is what makes honest cars trip the US position-consistency check. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-calibration"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.calibration` | string | | | recommended data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot.yaml when present; unset uses provisional built-in values. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | A `v2xw.bsm_timing.v1` calibration file (YAML), as the real-data pipeline writes it (`data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot.yaml`). Unset is the built-in values, which are PROVISIONAL (CV-pilot sample statistics). A timing calibration file fitted to real CV-pilot messages. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-locked-share"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.locked_share` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended 0.25 (Tampa CV pilot, built in); sweep 0 to 1. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The share of OBUs in the `locked` class (secMark on the GNSS fix epoch), 0 to 1; the other classes share the rest in proportion. Unset is the calibration's own share (0.25 built in: Tampa's 48 locked of 190 classified IDs). The share of cars whose message time is locked to the GPS fix. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-enabled"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.enabled` | boolean | | | recommended Off (default) keeps earlier runs; on for the most realistic locked-unit timing (CV-pilot Tampa and Wyoming units). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Turns the chain on. Unset or false is off. Locked units report the position of the GPS fix itself and stamp the message on the fix or one millisecond early, switching between the two as real units do; when a unit switches to early its position often takes a small lasting step. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-profile"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.profile` | string | | | `tampa_locked`, `wyoming_obu`, `tampa_chain`<br>recommended tampa_chain with data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot-chain-device.yaml for the closest out-of-sample match to Wyoming; tampa_locked is the default. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The rate set: `tampa_locked` (default; Tampa's locked IDs, a fit set), `wyoming_obu` (the one Wyoming OBU, P1-E4's held-out source) or `tampa_chain` (Tampa's chain devices alone, steps out of state 0 only; use it with `data/calibration/bsm-timing-cvpilot-chain-device.yaml`). Which real units' switching rates to use: Tampa's locked units (stamped early on about 10 % of messages), the Wyoming unit (46 %), or Tampa's switching units alone (tampa_chain, 26 %, whose positions step only while stamped on the fix; use it with the chain-device timing file). |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-stay-minus1"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.stay_minus1` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended Unset (the profile's: 0.235 Tampa, 0.566 Wyoming). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | P(the next BSM is stamped 1 ms early &#124; this one is); unset is the profile's. The chance that a message stamped early is followed by another early one. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-stay-zero"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.stay_zero` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended Unset (the profile's: 0.918 Tampa, 0.630 Wyoming). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | P(the next BSM is stamped on the epoch &#124; this one is); unset is the profile's. The chance that a message stamped on the fix is followed by another on the fix. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-steps"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.steps` | boolean | | | recommended On (default) with the chain. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Lasting position steps at 0 -&gt; -1 transitions, at the profile's rate and size. Unset is true. Whether a switch to early stamping can carry a lasting position step of a few centimetres, as the real units' positioning filter does. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-speed-per-m"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.speed_per_m` | number | m/s per m | | [-5, 5]<br>recommended Unset (no speed change; it barely moves the position check but matters for speed-consistency detectors); 0.499 for Tampa's switching units. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The reported speed's change with a step, m/s per m of along-track step. Unset is no speed change; set, it turns the change on (Tampa's chain devices: 0.499). How much the reported speed jumps, in m/s per metre, when a unit's position takes a step; the jump then fades. Real units' speed steps with their position. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-speed-tau-s"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.speed_tau_s` | number | s | | (0, 60]<br>recommended Unset (Tampa's 0.357 s). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The speed change's decay time, s; unset is Tampa's 0.357 (needs `speed_per_m`). How quickly the speed jump that comes with a step fades. |
| <span id="s-actors-vehicles-bsm-timing-stamp-chain-position-follows"></span>`actors.vehicles.bsm_timing.stamp_chain.position_follows` | number | | | [0, 1]<br>recommended Unset (Tampa's 0.759). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The share of the speed change the reported position moves with, 0 to 1; unset is Tampa's 0.759 (needs `speed_per_m`). How much of the speed jump the reported position follows: 1 moves the position with the reported speed, 0 leaves it on the old speed. |

## vru

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| <span id="s-actors-vru-pedestrians"></span>`actors.vru.pedestrians` | integer | people | `0` | recommended 0 to 400 at once. | basic | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | How many pedestrians. People walking on the sidewalks and crossings. Those with a phone or wearable can broadcast their own safety messages (PSM). *Status: Pedestrians walk sidewalks and cross streets on crosswalk lanes (social-force model), and away from them: with the default 'observed' behaviour they walk at speeds by age group (Knoblauch et al. 1996), step off after a start-up time when walk comes on, cross against flashing or steady don't-walk when they are among the share who do and the gap passes the HCM critical headway (calibrated to Midtown counts, Basch et al. 2015), walk in groups, and cross mid-block (jaywalk, straight or diagonal) where blocks are long, more often beside stopped traffic, with a lane-by-lane gap. Vehicles yield to anyone on a crosswalk, stop for anyone in or about to enter their lane mid-block, a few yield to a pedestrian waiting at the kerb, and never stop inside a crosswalk. Signalised crosswalks get MUTCD walk, flashing don't-walk (3.5 ft/s clearance) and don't-walk intervals. Cyclists ride the lanes that admit bicycles at naturalistic speeds (conventional and e-bike, Schleinitz et al. 2017). Partial because: crossing nodes with no crossing way get no crosswalk, the grid has no separate cycle lanes, and a cyclist rides the lane centre.* |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-cyclists"></span>`actors.vru.cyclists` | integer | people | `0` | recommended 0 to 150 at once. | basic | :material-circle-half-full:{ title="Partly active" } `partial` | How many cyclists. People riding bicycles and e-bikes among the traffic. *Status: Pedestrians walk sidewalks and cross streets on crosswalk lanes (social-force model), and away from them: with the default 'observed' behaviour they walk at speeds by age group (Knoblauch et al. 1996), step off after a start-up time when walk comes on, cross against flashing or steady don't-walk when they are among the share who do and the gap passes the HCM critical headway (calibrated to Midtown counts, Basch et al. 2015), walk in groups, and cross mid-block (jaywalk, straight or diagonal) where blocks are long, more often beside stopped traffic, with a lane-by-lane gap. Vehicles yield to anyone on a crosswalk, stop for anyone in or about to enter their lane mid-block, a few yield to a pedestrian waiting at the kerb, and never stop inside a crosswalk. Signalised crosswalks get MUTCD walk, flashing don't-walk (3.5 ft/s clearance) and don't-walk intervals. Cyclists ride the lanes that admit bicycles at naturalistic speeds (conventional and e-bike, Schleinitz et al. 2017). Partial because: crossing nodes with no crossing way get no crosswalk, the grid has no separate cycle lanes, and a cyclist rides the lane centre.* |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-device-fraction"></span>`actors.vru.device_fraction` | number | | `0.0` | [0, 1]<br>recommended 0 to 0.5; few phones broadcast V2X today. | basic | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | What fraction of them carry a device that transmits. The share of pedestrians and cyclists carrying a device that sends V2X messages. |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-behaviour"></span>`actors.vru.behaviour` | string | | `observed` | `observed`, `document` | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | How the pedestrians behave: `observed` (the default — walking speeds by age group, start-up at walk, a share who cross against the signal into a gap, groups, and mid-block crossing) or `document` (the 1995 social-force defaults, Helbing &amp; Molnár 1995: one speed law, everyone waits for walk, nobody crosses mid-block). |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-midblock-rate-per-100m"></span>`actors.vru.midblock_rate_per_100m` | number | per 100 m | | [0, 100] | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Overrides the observed behaviour's mid-block crossing rate, decisions per 100 m of eligible sidewalk walked; 0 turns mid-block crossing off. |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-red-crossing-share"></span>`actors.vru.red_crossing_share` | number | | | [0, 1] | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Overrides the observed behaviour's share of pedestrians who cross against the signal when the traffic leaves a gap. |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-ebike-share"></span>`actors.vru.ebike_share` | number | | | [0, 1] | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Overrides the share of cyclists on e-bikes. |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-crossing-gap-margin-s"></span>`actors.vru.crossing_gap_margin_s` | number | s | | [0.5, 6] | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Overrides the median time a pedestrian wants a traffic gap to leave beyond the time to walk across (the HCM's start-up and clearance time), seconds. |
| <span id="s-actors-vru-walking-speed-mps"></span>`actors.vru.walking_speed_mps` | number | m/s | | [0.5, 2.5]<br>recommended 1.51 m/s (Knoblauch 1996 crosswalk study); 1.2 to 1.6 m/s. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Overrides the mean walking speed of pedestrians under 65, m/s. Under `observed` the 65-and-over mean scales with it (keeping Knoblauch et al. 1996's ratio, 1.25 against 1.51 m/s); under `document` it is the one Gaussian's mean (1.34 m/s). How fast pedestrians under 65 walk on average; older walkers are slower in proportion. Slower walkers need longer gaps and longer crossing time. |

## Deployment

Which certificate system runs and how it is laid out: the providers on the trust list, the electors who sign that list, and the parts of the design the US does not deploy. Leave it on "US system (2025)" for the real deployment. Any change the US does not make is marked not US and recorded in the run's manifest.

| Setting | Type | Unit | Default | Range or choices | Level | Status | Description |

The credential system the backend runs; it must match the one the vehicles use. Model slot: family `protocol`, see [model parameters](models.md). |

| <span id="s-actors-backend-links-to"></span>`actors.backend.links[].to` | string | | | `ra`, `pca`, `la1`, `la2`, `ma`, `crlg`, `lop`, `crl_store`, `crl_broadcast`, `eca`, `dcm`<br>recommended A server role. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The entity it ends at. The other end of the link. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-links-latency-ms"></span>`actors.backend.links[].latency_ms` | number | ms | | [0, ∞)<br>recommended 10 ms (the engine's default backend link). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | One-way latency, milliseconds. The link's one-way latency. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-links-capacity-mbps"></span>`actors.backend.links[].capacity_mbps` | number | Mbit/s | | (0, ∞)<br>recommended 1,000 Mbit/s (the engine's default backend link). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Capacity, megabits per second. The link's capacity. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-failures-node"></span>`actors.backend.failures[].node` | string | | | `ra`, `pca`, `la1`, `la2`, `ma`, `crlg`, `lop`, `crl_store`, `crl_broadcast`, `eca`, `dcm` (or another value)<br>recommended Pick the provider, then the server. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The server: a role (`pca`, `la1`, `la2`, `ma`, `crlg`, `ra`, …) or a committee member, `&lt;role&gt;-member-&lt;k&gt;` (`pca-member-0`, `linkage-member-2`, `crl-member-1`); the home provider's, unless qualified by its provider, `&lt;provider&gt;/&lt;role&gt;` (`provider-b/crlg`). The server that fails: a role of the home provider, another provider's (provider-b/crlg), or a committee member. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-failures-mode"></span>`actors.backend.failures[].mode` | string | | | `offline`, `slow`, `malicious`<br>recommended offline for an outage study. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `offline`, `slow` or `malicious`. How it fails: down (messages dropped), slow (extra time per message) or lying (invalid committee shares). |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-failures-from-s"></span>`actors.backend.failures[].from_s` | number | s | | [0, ∞)<br>recommended Inside the run. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | When it starts, s. When the failure starts, in seconds into the run. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-failures-to-s"></span>`actors.backend.failures[].to_s` | number | s | | [0, ∞)<br>recommended Unset, or after from_s. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | When it ends, s; absent for the rest of the run. When the server recovers; unset means it stays failed to the end. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-failures-extra-ms"></span>`actors.backend.failures[].extra_ms` | number | ms | | (0, 600000]<br>recommended 10 to 1,000 ms. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | For `slow`: the extra service time per message, ms. Under slow, the extra service time each message takes. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-availability-model"></span>`actors.backend.availability.model` | string | | `always-up` | `always-up`, `two-state`<br>recommended Always up; random outages to study how the SCMS rides out failures (a sensitivity sweep, not a measured figure). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `always-up` (the default) or `two-state`. Whether every backend server fails at random: its up times and repair times are drawn at random (exponential), and while down it is offline, so devices retry their requests. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-availability-mtbf-h"></span>`actors.backend.availability.mtbf_h` | number | h | `720.0` | [1, 87600]<br>recommended 720 h (a month; an assumption: no provider publishes its availability). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Mean time between failures, hours (720 unless set). The mean time a backend server runs between two random failures, in hours. Applies when `actors.backend.availability.model` is `two-state`. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-availability-mttr-min"></span>`actors.backend.availability.mttr_min` | number | min | `30.0` | [1, 10080]<br>recommended 30 min (an assumption). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | Mean time to repair, minutes (30 unless set). The mean time a failed backend server takes to come back, in minutes. Applies when `actors.backend.availability.model` is `two-state`. |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-service-time-model"></span>`actors.backend.service_time.model` | string | | `deterministic` | `deterministic`, `log-normal`<br>recommended Fixed; variable to see how service-time spread moves latency percentiles. | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | `deterministic` (the default) or `log-normal`. Whether each backend request takes the same time every time (the cost table) or a time that varies at random around it (log-normal, median the fixed time). |
| <span id="s-actors-backend-service-time-cv"></span>`actors.backend.service_time.cv` | number | σ/mean | `0.25` | [0, 3]<br>recommended 0.25 (an assumption: no provider publishes it). | advanced | :material-check-circle:{ title="Active" } `wired` | The multiplier's coefficient of variation (0.25 unless set). How widely backend service times spread: the coefficient of variation of the log-normal multiplier (0 is fixed, 1 as wide as an exponential). Applies when `actors.backend.service_time.model` is `log-normal`. |

## Choices

The labelled values of every closed or model setting above.

??? note "`actors.vehicles.demand.kind`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `mobility/demand/poisson` | Steady arrivals (Poisson) | Vehicles enter at random at the rate below, each with its own trip across the map. |
 | `mobility/demand/tr36885-drop` | 3GPP drop (TR 36.885) | Every vehicle placed at once at the 3GPP evaluation spacing; for radio benchmarks. |
 | `mobility/demand/none` | No vehicles | No vehicle demand: pedestrians, roadside units and the backend only. |
 | `mobility/demand/sumo-rou` | SUMO route file (.rou.xml) | Every vehicle, flow and vehicle type of a SUMO route file, each driven by its own type. |
 | `mobility/demand/routes` | Saved routes (v2xw/routes/1) | The trips and chosen routes a traffic assignment saved, run again as they are. |
 | `mobility/demand/trips` | Trip list | A list of trips, each with its own departure, origin and destination. |
 | `mobility/demand/od-matrix` | Origin-destination matrix | Trips drawn from a zone-to-zone matrix, as SUMO's od2trips draws them. |
 | `mobility/demand/counts` | Traffic counts | Routes and trips sampled to reproduce observed counts, as SUMO's routeSampler does. |
 | `mobility/demand/gtfs` | Transit timetable (GTFS) | Buses and trams on their scheduled routes, from a GTFS feed. |
 | `mobility/demand/purposes` | Trips by purpose | A day of home-based tours and other trips, each departing on its purpose's profile. |
 | `mobility/demand/composite` | Several demand models together | The trips of several demand models at once, for example commuters plus transit. |

 | `obu/generic-automotive-soc-no-hsm` | Generic automotive soc no hsm | |

??? note "`actors.vehicles.drivers.realism`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `calibrated` | Calibrated city drivers | Each driver their own free speed, reaction at a green and following style; tuned to HCM saturation flow. |
 | `identical` | Identical (textbook model) | Every driver the same ideal model: the limit exactly, instant reactions. For model studies. |
 | `heterogeneous` | Heterogeneous | Calibrated, and each driver keeps their own gap and accelerates and brakes their own way. |
 | `human` | Human (reaction time and misjudgement) | Heterogeneous, with a 0.8 s reaction and misjudged gaps: dense traffic forms stop-and-go waves. |

??? note "`actors.vehicles.gnss.quality`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `reid-2019` | Production receiver, measured (3.07 m at 68 %) | Reid et al. 2019's fit of a production GNSS receiver, 3.07 m horizontal and 4.59 m vertical at 68 %; the default, because city runs are not open sky. |
 | `j2945-1` | SAE J2945/1 open sky (1.5 m / 3 m at 68 %) | A receiver that meets J2945/1's open-sky accuracies: 1.5 m horizontal and 3 m vertical at 68 %, speed 0.28 m/s, heading 2-3°, the heading held below 1.10 m/s. |
 | `rtk` | RTK (0.26 m) | An RTK-corrected receiver, 0.26 m at 68 % (Reid 2019's OxTS RT3000 rows). |

??? note "`actors.vru.behaviour`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |

 | `observed` | As observed in Midtown | Walking speeds by age, crossing against the signal and mid-block as field studies measured. |

??? note "`actors.rsus[].roles[]`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `report-forward` | Relay misbehaviour reports | Forwards vehicles' reports to the backend when they have no cellular link. |
 | `crl` | Broadcast the revocation list | Repeats the certificate revocation list on the air. |
 | `provisioning-proxy` | Deliver certificate top-ups | Carries pseudonym-certificate downloads for vehicles without cellular. |
 | `spat` | Signal timing (SPaT) and priority | Broadcasts the junction's signal state and answers emergency-vehicle requests. |
 | `map` | Intersection map (MAP) | Broadcasts the junction's lane geometry. |
 | `spat-map` | Signal timing and map | Both of the above. |
 | `cpm` | Infrastructure collective perception (CPM) | Its own cameras or radars watch the junction and it broadcasts what they see. |

??? note "`actors.rsus[].profile`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `rsu/cohda-mk5-rsu` | Cohda mk5 RSU | Roadside unit (Cohda MK5 RSU). |
 | `rsu/commsignia-its-rs4` | Commsignia its rs4 | Roadside unit (Commsignia ITS-RS4), the most complete public RSU datasheet found. |

??? note "`actors.rsus[].backhaul`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `backhaul/fixed` | Fixed line | A wired link with a set latency and capacity. |
 | `backhaul/fibre` | Fibre | Metro fibre to the backend: 1 Gbit/s and well under a millisecond. |
 | `backhaul/dsl` | DSL (copper) | A VDSL2 phone line: 20 Mbit/s up, 80 down, about 9 ms each way. |
 | `backhaul/microwave` | Microwave | A point-to-point radio hop: 400 Mbit/s, about 0.2 ms, rare outages. |
 | `backhaul/cellular` | Cellular | The unit reaches the backend over the mobile network. |
 | `backhaul/none` | None (offline) | The unit has no backend link. |

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `rsu/cohda-mk5-rsu` | Cohda mk5 RSU | |
 | `rsu/commsignia-its-rs4` | Commsignia its rs4 | |

??? note "`actors.backend.protocol`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `protocol/etsi/ts102941` | European CCMS (ETSI TS 102 941) | Authorization tickets, an enrolment authority and passive revocation. |
 | `protocol/scms/camp` | US SCMS (CAMP) | The US credential system: butterfly keys, two linkage authorities, linkage-value CRL. |

??? note "`actors.backend.entities.*.profile`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `backend/cloud-vm-x86` | Cloud vm x86 | Cloud VM class with software crypto only — the host-CPU bound for an SCMS or ETSI backend entity. |
 | `backend/hsm-appliance-luna7` | Hsm appliance luna7 | Network-attached HSM appliance (Thales Luna Network HSM 7, A750 enterprise tier). |
 | `bs/lte-macro-generic` | Lte macro generic | Generic LTE macro base station for the Uu top-up and report paths. |

??? note "`actors.backend.entities.*.service_model`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `service/mmc` | c parallel workers | The server runs the backend's worker count in parallel behind one queue (M/M/c, the default). |
 | `service/mm1` | One worker | The server handles one message at a time behind one queue (M/M/1). |

??? note "`actors.backend.entities.*.net`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `backend-net/fixed` | Fixed links | Links between backend authorities with a set latency and capacity. |

??? note "`actors.backend.entities.*.availability.model`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `always-up` | Always up | The server never fails at random; only actors.backend.failures windows take it down. |
 | `two-state` | Random outages (two-state) | The server fails after an exponential up time (mean MTBF) and is repaired after an exponential down time (mean MTTR); while down it is offline, as a failure window. |

??? note "`actors.backend.entities.*.service_time.model`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `deterministic` | Fixed (cost table) | Every request takes its cryptographic cost plus the fixed overhead, the same each time. |
 | `log-normal` | Variable (log-normal) | Each request's time is the fixed one times a log-normal draw with median 1 and the coefficient of variation below. |

??? note "`actors.backend.links[].from`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `ra` | Registration Authority | Takes devices' certificate requests, shuffles them and expands their butterfly keys. |
 | `pca` | Pseudonym CA (ACA) | Signs the pseudonym certificates vehicles broadcast with (IEEE 1609.2.1 calls it the ACA). |
 | `la1` | Linkage Authority 1 | Issues half of each certificate's linkage value, so no single authority can link a vehicle's pseudonyms. |
 | `la2` | Linkage Authority 2 | Issues the other half of each certificate's linkage value. |
 | `ma` | Misbehaviour Authority | Receives misbehaviour reports, investigates and orders revocations. |
 | `crlg` | CRL Generator | Signs and publishes the certificate revocation list. |
 | `lop` | Location Obscurer Proxy | Hides a device's network address from the RA with one extra hop; CAMP design only, not US. |
 | `crl_store` | CRL Store | Serves the CRL to devices that fetch it; CAMP design only, not US. |
 | `crl_broadcast` | CRL broadcast | Pushes the CRL to roadside units that repeat it on the air; CAMP design only, not US. |
 | `eca` | Enrolment CA | Issues each device's enrolment certificate once, when it is built or installed. |
 | `dcm` | Device Configuration Manager | The device's point of contact for enrolment and certificate downloads. |

 |---|---|---|

 | `crl_broadcast` | CRL broadcast | Pushes the CRL to roadside units that repeat it on the air; CAMP design only, not US. |
 | `eca` | Enrolment CA | Issues each device's enrolment certificate once, when it is built or installed. |
 | `dcm` | Device Configuration Manager | The device's point of contact for enrolment and certificate downloads. |

??? note "`actors.backend.failures[].mode`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `offline` | Down | The server is offline for the window: every message delivered to it is dropped. |
 | `slow` | Slow | Each message takes the extra time below on top of its service time, for the window. |
 | `malicious` | Lying | A committee member sends invalid threshold shares; only a committee member can lie. |

??? note "`actors.backend.availability.model`"

 | Value | Label | Meaning |
 |---|---|---|
 | `always-up` | Always up | The server never fails at random; only actors.backend.failures windows take it down. |
 | `two-state` | Random outages (two-state) | The server fails after an exponential up time (mean MTBF) and is repaired after an exponential down time (mean MTTR); while down it is offline, as a failure window. |
